briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B in Sales as Repeal Bill Drops; DEA Nears a Verdict, Psychedelics Sprint to FDA
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market just crossed $17 billion in cumulative sales even as operators fight the 24% wholesale tax with a new repeal bill and supplier cost-sharing deals. Nationally, the DEA's rescheduling hearing record is locked and awaiting a judge's call, while FDA-fast-tracked psilocybin and a wave of MSO M&A signal real momentum for the industry heading into Q4.

local.text: Michigan crosses $17 billion in lifetime sales
local.detail: State data shows combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales have surpassed $17 billion since regulated sales began, with August alone bringing in roughly $259 million.
local.text_full: Michigan crosses $17 billion in lifetime sales — State data shows combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales have surpassed $17 billion since regulated sales began, with August alone bringing in roughly $259 million.

local.text: Lawmaker files bill to kill the 24% wholesale tax
local.detail: A Republican state representative introduced House Bill 6224 to repeal the wholesale tax outright, calling it an unnecessary burden on operators.

local.text: Jars Cannabis forces removal of surveillance camera
local.detail: The Madison Heights store got city officials to take down a parking-lot-facing Flock camera that had been required under a 2022 licensing settlement.

local.text: Muskegon's dispensary-restaurant hybrid readies fall launch
local.detail: Fields Cannary is targeting a fall opening for its retail cannabis dispensary, with a full-service restaurant to follow — a hospitality-forward format ahead of most Michigan stores.

local.text: Tax squeezes U.P. chain, but a rival finds the fix
local.detail: Higher Love closed five of its nine Upper Michigan stores citing the 24% tax, while competitor Rize kept growing by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements that split the tax burden with suppliers.

national.detail: With the record now locked, Chief ALJ Derek Julius is next up to issue a recommended decision on whether marijuana qualifies for Schedule III.
Compass Pathways, Usona Institute and Transcend Therapeutics each landed a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher, cutting standard FDA review time from about a year to just one to two months.

national.text: Compass Pathways eyes psilocybin approval by year-end
national.detail: Journey Clinical, which is prepping treatment sites in Virginia, says it expects FDA approval of Compass's COMP360 by year's end with a potential 2027 rollout.

national.text: Vireo Growth's buying spree hits 265 stores nationwide
national.detail: Vireo's all-stock merger with Planet 13 adds 36 dispensaries across three states, pushing its footprint toward roughly 265 stores across 15 states.

national.text: Curaleaf presses $1.5B hostile bid for Aurora
national.detail: Curaleaf launched a shareholder campaign urging Aurora investors to tender into its 45%-premium takeover offer, pitching a combined company with over $1.5B in revenue and $40M in cost synergies.
